Signal is price-based only so estimate restatements cannot contaminate it.

Either prediction failing is informative. ETFs used because a single-stock version is survivorship-poisoned (E3 lesson).
nodes.norm_label: never-book-a-loss deep-dip strategy (buy ≤0.80×ath, sell +15%, no stop)

nodes.label: Post-Hoc Universe-Narrowing Prohibition
nodes.rationale: broad_us alone cleared all four criteria but this does NOT rescue E1: the pre-registered experiment was the full 29-ETF universe and it FAILED. Selecting broad_us after seeing results is post-hoc narrowing, forbidden by prereg §10 — it becomes a NEW hypothesis (E1b) under its own dated pre-registration. A lead, not a result.

nodes.label: Overnight Gap Component of the Mean-Reversion Edge
nodes.rationale: Measured: 54% of the close-to-close IBS edge lives in the close→next-open gap (6.3 of 11.8 bps pooled); next-open execution keeps ~64% of the edge because reversion continues into a second night. Many single-country ETFs' IBS edge is a stale-NAV/overnight artifact a next-open loop cannot harvest. This gap between 'the effect is real' and 'you can capture it at next open' became the story of the entire project.
nodes.norm_label: overnight gap component of the mean-reversion edge

nodes.label: E1 Power Calculation (M1.6, signal frequency)
nodes.rationale: E1 is signal-abundant and capacity-constrained (19.6% of bar-days signal; ~1,431 signal-days/yr): the limit is concurrency, not signals. Integrity note: no post-signal returns computed before the pre-registration commit. Honest caveat: frequency ≠ edge.

nodes.rationale: The engine sizes at fixed initial-capital/K dollars, not current-NAV/K — after losses it keeps buying full size (implicit leverage); at K=1 in 3× funds NAV crossed zero (104% maxDD). Immaterial for E1/E1b, does not change the E2 gate verdict; recorded as a known limitation, not silently fixed post-hoc. Any future engine must size on current NAV.

nodes.label: Regime Flattery (leverage × a secular bull)
nodes.rationale: 3× Nasdaq over 2014–2026 is leverage on the best tech decade in history; the base engine is 'leverage × a secular bull'. Discount forward expectations hard — the +2.45%/mo is a backtest ceiling, not a forecast. This flag directly motivated E5's hostile-regime test.

nodes.rationale: Synthetic daily-rebalanced 3× Nasdaq with 4.00%/yr calibrated drag reproduces real TQQQ to 0.05pp CAGR — so extending the test to 2000–2013 (before TQQQ existed) is a legitimate test, not an artifact.

nodes.label: Whipsaw Failure Mode in Secular Bear Markets
nodes.rationale: In choppy secular bears (2000–2002, 2008) violent counter-trend rallies push price back above the 200-day MA, the strategy re-enters 3× leverage, and the next leg down destroys it — repeatedly. The 200-MA did not protect: 92.7% drawdown 2000–2013.
nodes.norm_label: whipsaw failure mode in secular bear markets

nodes.label: 1× 200-MA Drawdown-Management Overlay
nodes.rationale: Real, robust effect: improves Sharpe in every regime and roughly halves worst drawdown (83%→52%) by sitting in cash through crashes. But NOT the high-return goal — full-period CAGR 8.04% vs QQQ's 7.92%; the value is almost entirely drawdown reduction. 2× is not worth it (Sharpe below 1×, 80% DD back); the sweet spot is 1×.

nodes.rationale: E10 nuance: PEAD is the only experiment in the program to beat both benchmarks in the hostile 2000–2013 regime (+5.93%/yr while its universe lost money), but decayed post-2014 — 'real but small and decayed', still a decisive FAIL for high return. E12's instructive mechanism: waiting for confirmation did WORSE than raw dip-buying because the confirmation bar surrenders exactly the reversal pop that holds the edge — the same overnight-gap arithmetic that killed the IBS family.

nodes.label: Program Falsification Conclusion (0 PASS / 13 pre-registered attempts / 6 families)
nodes.rationale: Every codifiable strategy from both the Reddit thread and the five-article set is tested and falsified under pre-registration: no robust high-return EOD edge in anything tested at retail scale. Families: index mean reversion, leveraged trend, stock momentum, breakout, deep-dip accumulation, event-driven/PEAD.

nodes.label: E3 Concentrated Stock Momentum Results — FAIL (clean)
nodes.rationale: Failed the 15% return bar by a wide margin (6.27%) WITH survivorship + lookahead bias helping it, and momentum selection underperformed equal-weight buy-hold of its own universe in every window — the selection itself destroyed value. Closes the third and last plausible route (after mean reversion and leveraged trend) to a high-return executable retail edge.
nodes.norm_label: e3 concentrated stock momentum results — fail (clean)

nodes.label: Asymmetric-Falsification Framing (only a FAIL is interpretable)
nodes.rationale: On a survivorship- and lookahead-biased universe the biases can only INFLATE results, so a FAIL is clean and interpretable while a PASS would be uninterpretable (it would route to forward live paper instead). Inherited by E10.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric-falsification framing (only a fail is interpretable)

nodes.label: E7 International Validation Results — BOTH ARMS FAIL
nodes.rationale: The clean close: the one credible untested high-return idea (a-priori vol-gated 3× rotation) was tested on five genuinely unseen non-US regimes with knobs fixed before seeing data and failed every gate. Downgrades E6 too: the 1× overlay is real but market-dependent (works in Japan/Germany/HK/US, hurts risk-adjusted return in UK/Australia) — a useful-in-some-regimes tool, not a universal law.
nodes.norm_label: e7 international validation results — both arms fail

nodes.label: 3× Leverage Single-Day Wipeout Tail Risk (1987 Hang Seng)
nodes.rationale: The 1987 Hang Seng crash (>33% in one day) drives any 3× daily-rebalanced fund to zero permanently; no timing overlay can recover from a single-day wipeout. A mathematical, not statistical, argument against extreme leverage.
nodes.norm_label: 3× leverage single-day wipeout tail risk (1987 hang seng)

nodes.label: E8+E9 Results — Both FAIL (squeeze breakout; never-book-a-loss audit)
nodes.rationale: E8: compression predicts expansion, not direction — 31–38% win rate with no tail winners large enough to carry it. E9: both pre-registered predictions confirmed — 100% realized win rate (0 losses in 53 trades) coexisting with 3.46% gate CAGR, a −79.7% unrealized position, a 17-year underwater hold, and 38% dead capital; the win-rate statistic measures bookkeeping, not performance.
nodes.norm_label: e8+e9 results — both fail (squeeze breakout; never-book-a-loss audit)

Known caveats stated up front: published effects are close-to-close so next-open execution forfeits the overnight component; edge is small per trade so cost modeling is decisive; public signal so expect decay.

nodes.label: Terminal Finding — decorrelation is not the scarce resource, EDGE is
nodes.rationale: The final three attempts each cleared the <=0.30 correlation bar comfortably (GLD +0.089, TLT -0.191, pairs -0.057) and each failed profitability: an uncorrelated return stream is trivial to find at retail scale, one whose edge survives retail costs is not.

nodes.label: In-Sample-Composed Cap
nodes.rationale: A design composed after seeing prior results (M10-1, after 31) and that buys known survivors in crashes is a forward-paper hypothesis, not a live edge — the one design that actually CLEARED PASS-HR was still refused as a win.

nodes.label: M3 Forward Paper (Alpaca paper, live 2026-07-15)
nodes.rationale: The only lever producing uncontaminated (non-survivorship, non-in-sample) evidence; needs elapsed time rather than another attempt. Disclosed limitation: the three sleeves are ~one strategy — m10 runs the identical e6 rule on 69.7% of 4,226 sessions.

nodes.label: Overnight Gap (executioner #1)
nodes.rationale: The IBS/mean-reversion family loses >1/2 its edge to the overnight gap that a next-open EOD fill cannot capture (~54% component); only an intraday/MOC fill would capture it, and that is blocked by the EOD-only hard rule.

nodes.label: Turnover Cost (executioner #2)
nodes.rationale: Independently sinks what the gap leaves: ~93% of anomaly alpha dies under costs (Chen-Velikov), observed in-repo — only 1 of 5 decomposed FAILs was truly signal-dead.

nodes.label: 39-Name Survivor Large-Cap Universe
nodes.rationale: Deliberately biased in the strategy's favor to make FAILs decisive; M11 showed the bias is not merely a flattering tilt — the survivor set destroyed the documented bearish pattern edge by removing exactly the names a bearish pattern predicts.

nodes.label: E3 — Single-stock momentum (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: 6.27% gate CAGR, underperformed equal-weight buy-hold of its own survivor universe.

nodes.label: E6 — De-leveraged 1x moving-average trend rotation
nodes.rationale: PASS then downgraded: robust in the US but market-dependent (3/5 regions), cuts an 83% drawdown to ~52% at roughly market-level return — a drawdown-control overlay, explicitly NOT the high-return goal.

nodes.label: E8 — Volatility squeeze (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Compression predicts expansion, not direction (gate CAGR -1.43%).

nodes.label: E11 — Volume-gated breakout (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Volume gating adds nothing to the breakout signal.

nodes.label: E16 — Raw weekly reversal
nodes.rationale: Gate CAGR 16.76% — the only experiment to clear the 15% return bar — but on a 65.9% drawdown plus survivorship; EX-DECOMP measured a -4.96 pp gap bleed.

nodes.label: E18 — VIX term-structure overlay (weak PASS-RA)
nodes.rationale: The program's only PASS-RA and it is weak; gate is VIX/VIX3M < 1 (contango). A forward-paper candidate, not a live claim.

nodes.label: X1 — Volatility gate vs plain 200-DMA (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Confirms no vol gate beats the plain 200-DMA.

nodes.label: X2/X2b — Short-interest days-to-cover anomaly
nodes.rationale: Real and correctly signed (+18.4% / Sharpe 0.98 frictionless) but structurally uncapturable: properly costed it collapses to 9.2% / 0.56 at 5% borrow, the pure short is negative at every borrow level, and it requires shorting — impossible at $100-1,000 with no fractional shorting. X2's initial write-up over-weighted the frictionless number; X2b corrected it and the record preserves both.

nodes.label: X6 — Crypto BTC/ETH dual-MA trend pilot (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Crushes HODL in the 2018-22 bears (29.6% vs 4.3%, DD 82%->61%) but loses HODL's Sharpe in the 2023+ bull (0.76 < 1.01) — reproduces E6's lesson in a new domain: trend is drawdown control, not a return enhancer over buy-and-hold.
nodes.norm_label: x6 — crypto btc/eth dual-ma trend pilot (fail)

nodes.label: X7 — HYG:IEF credit-regime gate (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: The first gate ever to BEAT the plain 200-DMA in a window (GFC gate Sharpe 0.98 vs 0.61 — credit led 2008, so it de-risked earlier), then collapses in the 2014+ bull (3.81% / DD 47.6% / Sh 0.34, 221 whipsaw switches). A crisis specialist that self-destructs in bulls.

nodes.label: X8 — Non-equity trend on GLD/TLT (FAIL both arms)
nodes.rationale: Judged on an explicitly-labelled DIVERSIFIER bar declared before results. GLD is a 3-of-4 near-miss (Sharpe beat buy-hold in GATE, lost in SEC — the 6th one-window death); TLT's negative CAGR is materially understated by dividend-UNADJUSTED prices, a declared bias.
nodes.norm_label: x8 — non-equity trend on gld/tlt (fail both arms)

nodes.label: X9 — Gatev distance pairs / market-neutral relative value (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: The zero-cost diagnostic splits the failure: gross gate Sharpe 0.43, gross SEC -0.05 — the edge had already decayed BEFORE costs, then ~81 round trips/yr x ~20 bps ~= 16%/yr of drag finished it. 87.4% of trades converged: the mechanism works, the reversion is simply smaller than four legs of transaction cost.
nodes.norm_label: x9 — gatev distance pairs / market-neutral relative value (fail)

nodes.label: M10-1 Nagel Switch (in-sample-composed PASS-HR)
nodes.rationale: VIX>20 -> C1 residual reversal, VIX<=20 -> E6 trend. The program's FIRST PASS-HR (gate 17.87% / DD 59.95% / Sh 0.66) but composed after 31 results, survivor-flattered, DD clears by 0.05 pp, breaks at VIX>18 and at 15 bps, fails PASS-RA — forward-paper-only, not clean.

nodes.label: M10-2 — 2x QQQ stress mean-reversion (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Gate 2.99% CAGR / 83.3% DD, and it closes the E2 'c2c mirage': the 5-day hold neutralized the overnight gap (c2c 3.18% ~= next-open 2.99%), proving the gap was hiding a falling 2x knife into 2000-02/2008, not alpha.

nodes.label: M11 — Chart-pattern geometry (FAIL, signal-dead)
nodes.rationale: Rule-based (NOT LLM) causal detection of long-side reversal shapes; the last untested classical mechanism, chosen because every other strategy trades a NUMBER and none trades SHAPE. Gate -0.14% CAGR / Sh 0.09 with frictionless Rung B ~= 0. Payload: the survivor universe destroyed the documented bearish pattern edge (fwd-20 +1.70% vs unconditional +1.15%, the opposite of Savin 2007).

nodes.label: M12 2x2 Controlled Factorial (Horizon x Concentration)
nodes.rationale: Reporting the two main effects plus the interaction is the entire point; running only the both-relaxed cell would have said nothing about WHICH relaxation mattered, which was the objection to 'both at once'.

nodes.label: Horizon factor H (10 vs 63 sessions)
nodes.rationale: Cost drag is the program's most repeated killer — X9 quantified it at ~16%/yr from ~81 round trips — and fewer, longer holds pay less toll.

nodes.label: Concentration factor K (3 vs 20)
nodes.rationale: The program's own Hou-Xue-Zhang explanation says a factor premium is a decile spread across many names that K=1-3 cannot express — this tests that assertion instead of continuing to assume it.

nodes.label: 12-1 cross-sectional momentum signal (t-252 to t-21)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because BOTH known endpoints used this family — it is the bridge between E3 and momentum_v2, deliberately not a new idea.

nodes.label: momentum_v2 (Trading project, read-only reference)
nodes.rationale: Monthly horizon, K=50, VALIDATED (IS +21.0%/yr, OOS +26.5%/yr, OOS Sharpe 0.87) — the opposite-verdict endpoint to E3 in the same factor family.

nodes.label: OPEN universe decision (39 survivors / ~100 large-caps / Trading price_cache)
nodes.rationale: K=20 is only meaningful if the universe supports a real sort: top-20 of 39 is half the universe (tests direction, not magnitude). Recommended (b) ~100 large-caps — a genuine sort without coupling the two projects or inheriting price_cache's verified gaps (next_open 1.1M rows vs 15.7M close, only 3 delistings, median ticker 636 rows).
nodes.norm_label: open universe decision (39 survivors / ~100 large-caps / trading price_cache)

nodes.label: Diagnostic-not-deployment rule
nodes.rationale: Stated before any data is pulled because it is the easiest rule to break later: picking the best of four cells and deploying it IS in-sample composition — exactly the M10-1 mistake already capped. A winning cell requires a separate prereg on the D1 dual-bar before forward paper enters the conversation, and M12 cannot retroactively rewrite the search-phase terminal claim.

nodes.label: git tag search-phase-closed-v1 (6e8f431)
nodes.rationale: Declared revert point for the whole post-closure phase.

nodes.label: docs/trial_log.json
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable trial extraction; regenerate, never hand-edit. 37 prereg docs on disk, highest recorded attempt 38, 50 declared variants, 1 unresolvable field (E18 verdict) flagged rather than guessed.

nodes.label: scripts/build_trial_log.py
nodes.rationale: Must be re-run before every DSR computation; a stale log silently under-counts as soon as one more variant is tried. Emits null + _unknown for unresolvable fields and nothing downstream may fill them by inference.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Deflates an observed Sharpe by the number of trials the search actually conducted — the trial count is the single easiest input in the method to fudge, so a DSR run that does not read the trial log has no defensible count.

nodes.label: Declared-variants count is a LOWER BOUND
nodes.rationale: 50 counts only prereg-declared variants; it excludes parameter values explored before pre-registration, the ~90-method survey and dropped-16 list, and abandoned variants never written down. Therefore any DSR computed from 50 is OPTIMISTIC — the direction of error is stated so it cannot be quietly forgotten at the point of use.
nodes.norm_label: declared-variants count is a lower bound

nodes.label: UNRESOLVED 37-vs-38 attempt count
nodes.rationale: Not silently resolved, because picking one to make the arithmetic tidy is exactly what makes a trial count untrustworthy. Rule for DSR: use the LARGER figure — too high is more conservative, too low flatters the strategy; when in doubt the error must point away from significance.

nodes.label: headline_verdict_at_publication is a pointer, not a ruling
nodes.rationale: Several published verdicts were superseded (E4 PASS -> killed by E5; E6 PASS -> downgraded to a risk overlay; M10-1 PASS-HR -> capped in-sample-composed). final_verdict is deliberately null everywhere because it is not auto-derivable and the append-only record is authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: headline_verdict_at_publication is a pointer, not a ruling

nodes.label: Verdict-matcher prefix bug (m10_2 recorded as M10-1's PASS-HR)
nodes.rationale: The first matcher took the token before the first underscore, so m10_2_* matched M10-1's results doc and logged a FAIL as PASS-HR. A trial log that invents a verdict is worse than no trial log; the matcher now keeps numeric sub-indices and requires delimiters on both sides.
nodes.norm_label: verdict-matcher prefix bug (m10_2 recorded as m10-1's pass-hr)

nodes.label: [STANDING] fixed-policy sections
nodes.rationale: Cannot be weakened per-experiment; only their blanks are filled. A standing rule that genuinely cannot apply must be named in Disclosed Limitations with a dated reason, never silently dropped.

nodes.label: Tiered cost model (1 / 5 / 15-25 bps per side + 15 bps stress leg)
nodes.rationale: 1 bp broad-index ETFs, 5 bps single stocks and sector ETFs, 15-25 bps or EXCLUDE below the liquidity floor, 25 bps crypto (Alpaca taker). The stress leg runs alongside the headline so cost-fragility is visible rather than discoverable later.
nodes.norm_label: tiered cost model (1 / 5 / 15-25 bps per side + 15 bps stress leg)

nodes.label: Time-stop baseline (price/trailing stops must BEAT it)
nodes.rationale: Stops interact with the overnight gap, so a naive stop is not free; any stop variant is an ADDITIONAL arm that must beat the time-stop-only arm to be adopted, and both are reported.
nodes.norm_label: time-stop baseline (price/trailing stops must beat it)

nodes.label: Probe-first data discipline
nodes.rationale: For any NEW data source, confirm fetch + parse + coverage BEFORE the prereg; if messy or thin, record BLOCKED-ON-DATA and stop (the E17/E19 pattern).

nodes.label: Sizing defaults (capped fractional-Kelly, anti-martingale, no leverage)
nodes.rationale: lambda <= 1/2 (never full Kelly) or fixed-risk r = 1-2% of NAV; never average down a loser; leverage only when the experiment IS a leverage test with a pre-committed regime stop. Frozen in the prereg because changing size rules after results is tuning.
nodes.norm_label: sizing defaults (capped fractional-kelly, anti-martingale, no leverage)

nodes.label: LLM overlays are forward-only
nodes.rationale: Any LLM-scored signal is a treatment arm on the M3 live-paper control and never a historical backtest — training-cutoff look-ahead makes LLM backtests dishonest.

nodes.label: Split-adjusted / dividend-UNADJUSTED convention (auto_adjust=False)
nodes.rationale: Every price consumer honors it and the runner header states it; the gap it leaves (no total-return path) is a declared bias, most visibly in TLT and SPY buy-hold comparisons.

nodes.label: Signal at close, execute next open (EOD hard rule)
nodes.rationale: No intraday logic until an intraday data source exists — which is also why the overnight-gap component the program repeatedly loses cannot be captured.
nodes.norm_label: signal at close, execute next open (eod hard rule)

nodes.label: .e8e9_cache / price_cache OHLCV store
nodes.rationale: Gitignored cache; runners do no swing.db writes and honor read-only on the Trading project's caches.

nodes.label: FF3-stripped residual return signal (126d betas, 21d residual sum)
nodes.rationale: E16's exact engine with ONLY the ranking variable changed, so any difference is attributable to the residual construction. Window lengths fixed a priori, not tuned.
nodes.norm_label: ff3-stripped residual return signal (126d betas, 21d residual sum)

nodes.label: Fama-French 3-factor daily series (Ken French library)
nodes.rationale: Free CSV zip fetched once and cached (gitignored, like price caches). Market-wide only — no industry factor, a disclosed simplification versus BHLV.

nodes.label: Consolidated squeeze -> channel-breakout spec (20/10/40, K=5)
nodes.rationale: Parameters fixed a priori from the canonical Donchian/turtle construct, not tuned; a single consolidated spec by design to deny the multiple-testing degrees of freedom the family invites.

nodes.label: 29-ETF frozen universe (swing_bot.universe)
nodes.rationale: Survivorship-light (ETFs don't delist like stocks) but later-inception names (XLRE 2015, XLC 2018) thin the early gate window — disclosed.

nodes.label: 15% vol-target weighting overlay (w = min(1, 0.15/sigma_ann))
nodes.rationale: 15% target is a round number fixed a priori with no tuning; leverage capped at 1 and a 0.05 rebalance band avoids daily churn. Overlay = risk management, not the high-return goal.

nodes.label: Even-week FOMC cycle-time exposure rule
nodes.rationale: Exposure 1 in even cycle-weeks (t in [0,4],[10,14],[20,24],[30,34]), 0 otherwise; t>34 flat handles the 2020 cancelled-meeting gap conservatively and is pre-registered, not tuned.

nodes.label: data/fomc_announcement_dates.json (260 scheduled dates, 1994-2026)
nodes.rationale: Compiled from federalreserve.gov primary sources (fomchistorical{YEAR}.htm 1994-2020, fomccalendars.htm 2021+), unscheduled/emergency meetings excluded, spot-checked against press releases. No lookahead: the schedule is published ~a year ahead.

nodes.label: VIX/VIX3M contango gate on SVXY
nodes.rationale: E18's exact gate reused, so the experiment tests the carry instrument rather than a new timing rule.

nodes.label: -20% hard kill-switch + 21-session stand-down
nodes.rationale: Threshold and stand-down fixed a priori and untuned; modeled honestly so the exit eats the next-open gap. Overnight cascade risk remains structurally uncapped at EOD — the honest reason the verdict is PROMISING-capped at best.

nodes.label: Volmageddon 2018-02-05 (XIV termination)
nodes.rationale: Effective N ~= 1 for the tail; SVXY's -1x -> -0.5x regime change on 2018-02-27 is left in the actual traded prices with no synthetic splicing, so the backtest experiences what a holder experienced.

nodes.label: TOM 4-session window rule (-1, +1, +2, +3)
nodes.rationale: Standard McConnell-Xu definition, one calendar definition only — a robustness grid would be post-hoc tuning, so the a-priori window IS the test.

nodes.label: D1 Dual-Bar Verdict
nodes.rationale: Two independent acceptance tiers (high-return and risk-adjusted) fixed before every run so a result cannot be graded against a bar chosen after seeing it.

nodes.label: PASS-HR Tier (net CAGR >= 15%, maxDD <= 60%, both windows)
nodes.norm_label: pass-hr tier (net cagr >= 15%, maxdd <= 60%, both windows)

nodes.label: PASS-RA Tier (gate Sharpe >= 0.80, beats benchmark both windows)
nodes.norm_label: pass-ra tier (gate sharpe >= 0.80, beats benchmark both windows)

nodes.label: Asymmetric-Falsification Clause (only a FAIL is clean)
nodes.rationale: Survivorship can only help a long strategy, so a PASS on a survivor universe is uninterpretable and routes to forward paper; only a FAIL carries clean information.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric-falsification clause (only a fail is clean)

nodes.label: Modified-Window Cap (best verdict = PROMISING)
nodes.rationale: When a data floor makes the 2000-2013 gate impossible, only one window exists, so no PASS tier may be claimed; the ceiling is PROMISING pending forward confirmation.

nodes.label: M10 Data-Snooping Disclosure
nodes.rationale: M10 designs were composed after seeing 31-32 prior results on the same two windows; mitigations are a published pre-2012 switching mechanism, verbatim-inherited parameters, exactly one new number, and a cap on any in-window pass.

nodes.label: IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED, Forward Paper Required
nodes.rationale: A numerical pass on a design assembled from known survivors is not a clean pass; it is recorded as in-sample-composed and can only route to forward paper, never a live claim.

nodes.label: No Tuning a FAIL
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and parameters are fixed in the prereg before the run; a failing result is never re-tuned into a pass, and no post-hoc bolt-on de-risking is permitted.

nodes.label: Split-Adjusted / Dividend-UNADJUSTED Price Convention
nodes.rationale: auto_adjust=False across every consumer; stated as a mandatory header comment on any file touching prices so no consumer silently assumes total-return series.

nodes.label: EOD Rule: Signal at Close, Execute Next Open
nodes.norm_label: eod rule: signal at close, execute next open

nodes.label: Liquidity Floor (20-day dollar ADV >= $5M, price >= $5)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory at this capital size because spread/slippage dominate, but it structurally excludes the small illiquid hard-to-borrow names where the short-interest effect actually lives.

nodes.label: Decomposition Ladder A/B/C (c2c 0bps / next-open 0bps / next-open + cost)
nodes.rationale: Separates whether an apparent edge is signal-real, gap-dwelling, or cost-gated.
nodes.norm_label: decomposition ladder a/b/c (c2c 0bps / next-open 0bps / next-open + cost)

nodes.label: Tiered Cost Model (1 bp broad ETF / 5 bps single stock / 15 bps stress leg)
nodes.norm_label: tiered cost model (1 bp broad etf / 5 bps single stock / 15 bps stress leg)

nodes.label: Time-Stop Exit Baseline
nodes.rationale: Adopted as the baseline because C3 found time-stops beat channel exits; any price or trailing stop would have to beat the time-stop-only arm and none is adopted pre-emptively.

nodes.label: Opportunistic vs Routine Insider-Trade Classification
nodes.rationale: A purchase in month m is ROUTINE if the same insider also bought in month m in each of the three prior years, else OPPORTUNISTIC; CMP found only pattern-breaking trades carry information (~82 bps/mo), so E19 trades only the opportunistic subset.

nodes.label: Filing-Date Entry (point-in-time, no lookahead)
nodes.rationale: Entry uses the Form-4 filing date rather than the transaction date because the filing is what is publicly knowable at decision time (filed within 2 business days).

nodes.label: Dividend-Capture Ex-Date Accounting (D/P0 credit)
nodes.rationale: Because prices are dividend-UNADJUSTED, the ex-date drop would read as a pure loss unless the received dividend is credited to P&L; the per-trade return therefore adds a D/P0 term explicitly.

nodes.label: VIX > 20 Regime Switch (STRESS vs CALM)
nodes.rationale: The single new parameter in the M10 arc; 20.0 is the long-run VIX mean / canonical elevated line, sourced from Nagel's published pre-2012 mechanism rather than fit to these windows, with 18/22 reported to bound rather than tune.

nodes.label: C1 FF3-Residual Short-Term Reversal
nodes.rationale: Gate-alive but secondary-dead (19.08% to 2.92% CAGR); its own prereg already declared survivor-universe results uninterpretable.

nodes.label: E6 200-DMA Trend Rotation
nodes.rationale: Secondary-alive but gate-weak (2.66% to 14.47% CAGR) - window-disjoint from C1, which is why fixed-weight blends are arithmetically infeasible for PASS-HR.

nodes.label: E2 Leveraged IBS Mean-Reversion
nodes.rationale: Measured more than half its edge inside the signal-close-to-next-open gap: next-open CAGR 7.98% vs 18.15% close-to-close.

nodes.label: E3 Single-Stock Momentum (K=1-3, short hold) - FAIL
nodes.norm_label: e3 single-stock momentum (k=1-3, short hold) - fail

nodes.label: E18 VIX Term-Structure Gate
nodes.rationale: Cleared a weak PASS-RA but has worse drawdown than buy-hold in bull markets because it de-risks on any vol spike, including spikes inside an intact uptrend.

nodes.label: C3 Finding: Time-Stop Beats Channel Exit
nodes.norm_label: c3 finding: time-stop beats channel exit

nodes.label: X9 Turnover-Drag Quantification (~16%/yr over ~81 round trips)
nodes.norm_label: x9 turnover-drag quantification (~16%/yr over ~81 round trips)

nodes.label: EX-DECOMP Finding: Overnight Gap Is a Recurring Edge-Killer
nodes.norm_label: ex-decomp finding: overnight gap is a recurring edge-killer

nodes.label: momentum_v2 (Trading project, monthly hold, K=50) - VALIDATED
nodes.rationale: IS +21.0%/yr, OOS +26.5%/yr, OOS Sharpe 0.87 - same factor family as E3 but the opposite verdict, which is what makes the constraint question decisive.
nodes.norm_label: momentum_v2 (trading project, monthly hold, k=50) - validated

nodes.label: Gap Amortization via 5-Session Hold
nodes.rationale: E2's 1-day hold made the lost first-night gap ~100% of the capture window; a 5-day hold shrinks it to ~20% by holding days 2-5 of the reversion. Load-bearing assumption: if reversion completes on night 1 the extension recovers little.

nodes.label: Causal Pivot Detection (w=5 half-window, confirmed at j+w)
nodes.rationale: A swing high/low at bar j is only usable once w bars of right-side confirmation exist, so decision bar i sees only pivots with j+w <= i. LMW's two-sided kernel smoother is non-causal and is explicitly avoided as look-ahead.
nodes.norm_label: causal pivot detection (w=5 half-window, confirmed at j+w)

nodes.label: Fresh Upward Neckline Cross Entry Trigger
nodes.norm_label: fresh upward neckline cross entry trigger

nodes.label: Short-Side Diagnostic (reported, not gated)
nodes.rationale: Bearish mirrors are measured only to document the Savin (2007) short-side effect and confirm it is the non-deployable side - no fractional shorting at $100-1,000. A measurement, not a strategy, mirroring X2.

nodes.label: M11 Result: FAIL, Signal-Dead (gate -0.14% CAGR / Sharpe 0.09)
nodes.norm_label: m11 result: fail, signal-dead (gate -0.14% cagr / sharpe 0.09)

nodes.label: 12-1 Cross-Sectional Momentum (t-252 to t-21)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is the bridge signal between E3 (failed) and momentum_v2 (validated), not because it is a new idea - holding the signal constant is what makes the constraint factorial interpretable.

nodes.label: 2x2 Factorial: Horizon (10 vs 63 sessions) x Concentration (K=3 vs K=20)
nodes.rationale: Running only the doubly-relaxed cell could not attribute a result to either relaxation; reporting all four cells plus both main effects and the interaction is the entire point.
nodes.norm_label: 2x2 factorial: horizon (10 vs 63 sessions) x concentration (k=3 vs k=20)

nodes.label: H_0: Neither Constraint Binds
nodes.rationale: Written down before running precisely so it cannot be quietly discarded if the four cells come out flat.

nodes.label: M12 Verdict Discipline: Diagnostic, Not a Deployment Gate
nodes.rationale: Selecting the best of four cells and deploying it is in-sample composition - the documented M10-1 mistake. A real effect must be re-fixed in a separate prereg and gated on the standard D1 dual-bar before forward paper enters.
nodes.norm_label: m12 verdict discipline: diagnostic, not a deployment gate

nodes.label: Search-Phase Terminal Claim (37 attempts, no cost-surviving OOS edge)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly conditioned on the constraints (K=1-3, days-to-weeks holds, retail costs, free EOD data); M12 extends the map but cannot retroactively un-falsify anything already killed.
nodes.norm_label: search-phase terminal claim (37 attempts, no cost-surviving oos edge)

nodes.label: Existence Spread (low-minus-high DTC), Reported Not Deployable
nodes.rationale: Tests whether the documented sign exists at all in this universe, but is flagged non-deployable because the anomaly's alpha sits in the short (high-DTC) leg and there is no fractional shorting at this capital.
nodes.norm_label: existence spread (low-minus-high dtc), reported not deployable

nodes.label: 10-Session Dissemination-Lag Lookahead Guard
nodes.rationale: Short interest for settlement date S is not disseminated for ~8-9 business days, so entry waits 10 trading sessions past S - a fixed conservative approximation chosen to eliminate lookahead at the cost of signal freshness.

nodes.label: Conditional Volatility Targeting (de-risk only if vol elevated AND trend broken)
nodes.rationale: E18 de-risks on any vol spike including spikes inside an intact uptrend; requiring both conditions keeps the book invested through those, so the interaction must beat E6-alone and E18-alone on gate Sharpe to earn its keep.
nodes.norm_label: conditional volatility targeting (de-risk only if vol elevated and trend broken)

nodes.label: Purged K-Fold with Embargo (K=6, embargo 1%)
nodes.rationale: Labels built from forward windows leak into folds that touch those windows, so standard K-fold reports skill that does not exist; training observations overlapping a test label window are dropped, plus a 1% embargo after each test block.

nodes.label: CPCV (N=6 groups, 2 test groups, 15 combinations)
nodes.rationale: A single train/test split yields one path and one Sharpe - no distribution and no variance across paths; reporting the full distribution is mandatory because with concentrated books median and mean diverge sharply.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Adjusts an observed Sharpe for trial count, skew/kurtosis, and sample length; a strategy-level test of whether the Sharpe survives the number of trials searched.

nodes.label: Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO via CSCV)
nodes.rationale: Selection-level test: the fraction of splits where the in-sample-best configuration underperforms the median OOS. PBO > 0.5 means the selection procedure is worse than random - it measures selection, not edge.
nodes.norm_label: probability of backtest overfitting (pbo via cscv)

nodes.label: Measured Round-Trip Friction Model
nodes.rationale: Friction is the signed gap between the price the simulation assumed and the price actually obtained, computed per fill from live paper fills - never an assumed constant. It ships uncalibrated: n=4 fills cannot estimate a distribution, so it is an instrument, not a number.

nodes.label: Fail-Loud on Missing Measurement (MIN_FILLS_FOR_ESTIMATE = 20)
nodes.rationale: estimate_friction() raises rather than falling back to a constant or a defaulted warning; a caller may proceed only by passing an explicit assumed_bps, which stamps friction_source=ASSUMED on every downstream artifact so no report can present an assumption as a measurement.

nodes.label: Trial Count as Hard Input (larger of the two figures)
nodes.rationale: Read from trial_log.json, raising if missing or older than the newest prereg, because a stale log under-counts trials in exactly the direction that flatters the result; the 37-vs-38 discrepancy is resolved by erring toward more trials, and the count must print in the same block as the DSR.
nodes.norm_label: trial count as hard input (larger of the two figures)

nodes.label: Planted-Edge Falsifier (reported, not gated)
nodes.rationale: A harness that rejects everything is as useless as one that accepts everything, so a synthetic series with a genuinely predictable feature is fed in and must NOT be rejected; otherwise criteria 1-2 are satisfied trivially and the rejections carry no information.

nodes.label: Success Condition: The Harness Must REJECT Things
nodes.rationale: A validation layer that passes noise is not merely weak, it is harmful - it manufactures false confidence in exactly the situation it exists to prevent, so rejection of a worthless signal is pre-registered as the acceptance test before any code is written.
nodes.norm_label: success condition: the harness must reject things

nodes.label: Amended OR-Rule: Rejected if DSR Insignificant OR PBO >= 0.5
nodes.rationale: V1's AND-conjunction was mis-specified: DSR is strategy-level and PBO is selection-level, so requiring both demanded one strategy fail two unrelated tests. A no-edge rule with highly correlated variants has almost no selection to overfit, so its PBO sits near random while DSR correctly says no edge. Both statistics are still reported separately.
nodes.norm_label: amended or-rule: rejected if dsr insignificant or pbo >= 0.5

nodes.label: Amend by Superseding, Never by Rewriting the Original
nodes.rationale: V1 failed its own criterion 2 and that failure stands on the record; amending a criterion by rewriting the document it lives in would erase the evidence that it was ever wrong, which is the entire reason the project pre-registers anything.
nodes.norm_label: amend by superseding, never by rewriting the original

nodes.label: Predicted False Positive: Planted Edge Rejected via PBO 0.514
nodes.rationale: Written down in advance rather than explained away afterwards. Pre-committed handling: report it as a stated limitation of the selection-level axis - PBO is only meaningful when the configuration set represents a genuine selection choice - and do NOT loosen PBO_FAIL_AT or drop the falsifier; a V3 would compute PBO only over real selection sets.
nodes.norm_label: predicted false positive: planted edge rejected via pbo 0.514

nodes.label: Prereg X2b - Short-Side / Long-Short Days-to-Cover, Borrow-Costed
nodes.rationale: Follow-on to X2, which found the short-interest anomaly real but concentrated entirely on the high-DTC short leg and therefore non-deployable long-only; X2b asks the deployability question by costing borrow honestly.

nodes.label: Prereg X3 - Reg SHO Daily Short-Volume Drift

nodes.label: .e8e9_cache (second data layer, the research jungle)
nodes.rationale: Documented as a SECOND store distinct from swing.db (added to this bin 2026-08-13): gitignored, 292 files in ONE filename namespace over THREE shapes - 181 bar lists, 72 dicts (*_div, ff3_daily, *_idx, fred_*), 39 lists of date strings (*_earn). Only bar lists carry a vintage, so 111 entries are invisible to the freshness guard BY DESIGN. swing.db feeds the engines; this feeds the EXPERIMENTS.

nodes.label: Cache freshness contract (mixed / stale vintage)
nodes.rationale: 2026-08-12 (record EM/EO): entries are written on whatever day a ticker is first touched, so a universe assembled across sessions silently MIXES VINTAGES - that is what overstated M12's headline effect 3x. _note_vintage raises StaleCacheError on a mixed vintage (>=2 distinct end-dates in one process) or a stale one (> SWING_MAX_CACHE_STALE_DAYS, default 5 calendar days, measured against the CLOCK). Mixed fires BEFORE stale.

nodes.label: All-or-nothing cache refresh rule
nodes.rationale: The write path is per-ticker and cache-miss-driven, no script enumerates the cache, and no refresh tool exists (none should be built). Deleting a subset and re-running one consumer just manufactures a NEW mixed vintage: delete every price-series *.json and re-run every consumer in one sitting.

IBS=(close-low)/(high-low) divides by zero there, so signal code must skip a ticker on any high==low day (IBS undefined -> no signal) rather than crash. The other 28 universe tickers were clean.

nodes.label: A raise in a shared helper is inert until you check what CATCHES it
nodes.rationale: 2026-08-13 (record EO, measured): _note_vintage was changed 2026-08-12 to raise on a stale or mixed vintage and proved 5/5 in isolation, yet was swallowed at three reachable sites. Worst was cache_fetch's OWN retry loop - the call sat inside the try guarding prices.fetch, so a vintage verdict printed as '{ticker} attempt N error', slept 20/40/60/80s, refetched 4x and died as 'could not fetch'. run_m12_factorial and run_v1_harness_check caught it per-ticker and continued, so a uniformly stale cache excluded every name in turn: the guard turned 'refuse to run' into 'run on a silently emptied universe', strictly worse than the printing it replaced. Fixed by naming StaleCacheError(RuntimeError), moving the call out of the fetch try, and re-raising in both consumers. Rule: a broad except Exception around a call that can now raise a VERDICT must re-raise that verdict explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: a raise in a shared helper is inert until you check what catches it

nodes.label: scripts/ implicit namespace package -> two StaleCacheError classes
nodes.rationale: 2026-08-13 (record EQ, proven by identity not assumption): scripts/ has no __init__.py and the repo root is on sys.path, so 'import run_e8_squeeze' and 'import scripts.run_e8_squeeze' both succeed and produce TWO DIFFERENT module objects with two different StaleCacheError classes; 'except StaleCacheError' then silently does not match and the guard is swallowed again. Today's consumers are safe (m12 and v1 catch the identical class object, 'is' returns True; zero repo-wide hits for the dotted form). Applies to EVERY cross-script except in scripts/. Rule: import sibling scripts as bare run_x, never scripts.run_x.

nodes.label: market_is_open()
nodes.rationale: Audit finding #1 (critical): it FAILED OPEN - returned None on any AlpacaError and the caller then submitted orders anyway, defeating the intraday guard exactly when the broker is flaky (real Alpaca 500 on 2026-07-23). Now always returns a bool: Alpaca clock primary, local ET regular-hours fallback that errs safe.

nodes.label: fill_divergence Table
nodes.rationale: Audit finding #2 (high): it was INERT - 0-for-10 rows had a real fill price while the docstring claimed gaps are 'visible, never assumed'. Root cause was structural, not sloppy: submit rows carry the order id but a decision-day CLOSE as their sim side, realize rows carry the true sim fill but no order id, so the two halves could never be joined.

nodes.label: backfill_divergence()
nodes.rationale: The repair pass for the inert fill_divergence table: polls the real fill via get_order() and repairs sim_price from paper_transactions, backed by 2 additive columns.

nodes.label: Sim-vs-Broker Fill Fidelity Measurement
nodes.rationale: FIRST REAL FIDELITY NUMBERS: +0.0, +0.0, +1.3 bps when the EOD discipline held; -85.7 bps on the one run where it broke (the 07-20 midday fire). M3's premise that the DB ledger stands in for broker reality now has EVIDENCE rather than an assumption.
